transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-05
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (CSM), Martin (Vela), Priya (Vela), Lena (Vela), Aaron (Vela SRE)

Summary (auto): High-level health check: usage trends, cost spikes, reliability incidents, Q4 commit vs reserved capacity options, canary rollout plan for Dedicated pool. Action items captured.

Topics: usage growth and cost overruns, tail latency & p95 incidents, model selection for cost-sensitive routes, roadmap alignment on infra and compliance, next steps for pilot scaling.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Sophie (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'll kick off, we're on for about 50 minutes, just wanted to do a quick health check and then dive into the cost/uptime tradeoffs and next steps.
[00:00:12] Martin (Vela): Thanks, Sophie. Quick note, we only have 45-60 minutes from our side, Priya needs to drop at 16:00 local.
[00:00:20] Sophie: Got it, we'll prioritize the canary plan. Diego, do you want to start with the baseline we ran last week?
[00:00:28] Diego (Redwood SE): Sure — quick recap: we did the 12h sampling on your staging, synthetic traffic matching the 95th percentile. Observed average token cost ~0.0009 per token with current batch settings, p95 latency around 240ms for short-chat routes, but tail spikes to 1.2s under KV cache miss.
[00:00:50] Aaron (Vela SRE): That KV cache miss number is what bit us last month; memory pressure on our side, but also we saw spikes during the 3am batch jobs, maybe correlation.
[00:01:05] Priya (Vela): We're particularly sensitive to the p99 for our search ranking endpoint — if it crosses 2s we get cascading timeouts into our frontend.
[00:01:15] Diego: Understood. Two immediate levers: increase prefix caching (helps p99 on conversational flows) and lower max batch windows for that specific route to reduce latency at cost of throughput. We can also pin routing to a lighter-weight model for that route.
[00:01:34] Lena (Finance): When you say "cost of throughput" what ballpark increase are we talking? We need to present something to finance.
[00:01:40] Diego: From our sample, lowering batching for that route increased per-token cost ~6-9% but reduced p99 from 1.2s to ~0.55s. If you instead route to a quantized 70B variant you save ~12% per-token but add a 40-60ms single-request overhead. So it's tradeoffs.
[00:01:58] Martin: Can you repeat the quantized number? We heard "12%" — is that measured or estimate?
[00:02:05] Diego: It's a model-based estimate from our Optimize toolkit and the staging run metrics — conservative estimate, yields are about that when memory-bound but consistent across our profiles.
[00:02:18] Sophie: Quick interruption — on commitments: Sophie speaking as AE — we can give a quarter-tier reserved capacity proposal that includes a burst bucket; that helps smooth peak charges while giving a unit price reduction. I'll send tiers after the call.
[00:02:29] Lena: That's great. Is there a minimums lock or can we scale monthly? Our fiscal team prefers quarterly commitments.
[00:02:36] Sophie: We offer monthly flex tiers and quarterly/annual reserved discounts. The steepest discounts are annual, but quarterly reserved is fairly common for customers of your size. I'll include a Q4-focused option.
[00:02:45] [00:03:00] Maya (Redwood CSM): Also we'll include retention and audit log add-on pricing separately — I know you flagged needing longer audit logs earlier.
[00:03:07] Priya: Yes, compliance is important — 1 year of admin-level audit logs. Is that supported on Dedicated?
[00:03:12] Sophie: Yes, Dedicated and Private both support longer retention via our storage tiering; that'll be in the compliance appendix.
[00:03:20] Martin: Let's go deeper on reliability: we had two incidents in July, one correlated with the midnight ET batch and one with a model roll event. Can you explain fallback behavior if a model variant isn't available?
[00:03:32] Diego: Right — we support automated fallback to a compatible model variant or region route. For example, if your primary 70B quantized node is exhausted, policy can route to the unquantized 70B in another pool or to a 30B low-cost fallback. That does change LLM output fidelity, so it's a policy tradeoff.
[00:03:50] Aaron: The problem we saw was the fallback introduced a format regression — different tokenization caused downstream parser to mis-handle structured outputs.
[00:03:58] Diego: Good callout. For structured outputs we recommend function-calling guards + schema validation at the app layer, and we can also flag certain routes as "no-fallback" to ensure fidelity over availability.
[00:04:14] Sophie: For the QBR piece — what would success look like for you for the next quarter?
[00:04:19] Martin: Reduce monthly cost volatility by 25% and keep p99 below 800ms for ranking route. Also want a defined canary plan for production rollout of Dedicated pool.
[00:04:30] Priya: Add to that — we want a runbook for incidents that maps Redwood error codes to our SLO pages, and a way to trigger Redwood support escalation automatically.
[00:04:40] Sophie: We can provide an integration checklist for on-call escalation (pager + ticket playbook) and map those error codes.
[00:04:46] [00:05:10] Diego: On canary plan — proposed approach: 1) small-cap reserved staging pool with identical model variant; 2) traffic shadowing for two weeks; 3) incremental 5-10% traffic shifts with health checks (latency, error rate, model quality checks); 4) automatic rollback if quality regressions exceed threshold.
[00:05:30] Priya: For the shadowing — will that double our staging cost? We don't have budget for prolonged shadowing.
[00:05:36] Diego: We can run selective shadowing on a sampled traffic slice (e.g., 2-5%) that gives statistically meaningful signal without doubling cost.
[00:05:45] Martin: How do you measure quality regressions automatically? We have a small eval harness but it's noisy.
[00:05:52] Diego: We use prompt-level tests plus an evaluation set you provide; Redwood Optimize will run automatic regression checks and alert on drift vs baseline. For structured outputs, we run schema-level comparisons and sampling.
[00:06:05] Lena: Are there extra charges for Optimize?
[00:06:08] Sophie: Optimize is an add-on — some features included in the enterprise pack; we'll call out what's in your entitlement vs add-on.
[00:06:14] [00:06:45] Martin: On the cost side — looking at June-July we saw 38% month-on-month growth; some of that is feature adoption but we also have heavy peak bursts tied to our ingest pipeline. Can Redwood help smooth bursts?
[00:06:56] Diego: A couple of features: token pre-warming for predictable inference patterns, prefix caching, and burst capacity attached to reserved pools. Also, smart routing can shift some traffic to cheaper model variants during non-critical windows — schedule-based routing.
[00:07:10] Priya: Token pre-warming — explain in lay terms, I think engineers will like a demo.
[00:07:15] Diego: It's basically pre-warming KV cache for expected prefixes so initial requests are served from warm caches; reduces cold-start-like latency and amortizes cost. We'll demo in the follow-up.
[00:07:25] Aaron: Any hardware-level knobs? We run on heterogeneous GPUs and some of our nodes are older cards which are slower.
[00:07:31] Diego: Yes, model routing by hardware tier is supported. You can prefer newer cards for low-latency routes and use older ones for background or batch inference. That is part of Dedicated configuration.
[00:07:40] [00:07:58] Maya (CSM): Quick check — do we have any compliance docs pending? I think Vela asked for SOC 2 and encryption details last run.
[00:08:05] Priya: Yes, and KMS/HSM integration details — legal needs that to complete procurement.
[00:08:10] Sophie: We'll attach SOC 2, ISO, and KMS/HSM integration notes to the security appendix. I'll ask solutions to include a short HSM integration diagram.
[00:08:18] Martin: Great.
[00:08:30] [00:08:50] Diego: Back to incidents — two operational proposals: 1) set a stricter autoscale headroom for your reserved pool during known batch windows; 2) schedule maintenance windows that align with your batch processing to avoid cascading backpressure.
[00:09:05] Aaron: That aligns. We can shift some heavy batch to 02:00 UTC instead of 03:00, that's doable.
[00:09:11] Sophie: OK — time check, Priya needs to go at 16:00, let's surface immediate blockers: Priya?
[00:09:20] Priya: Budget OK for a small Q4 reserved trial but legal needs procurement checklist; also we need a short SLA summary for internal stakeholders.
[00:09:28] Sophie: We'll send a 1-pager SLA summary + procurement checklist.
[00:09:34] [00:09:50] Diego: I'll note the technical blockers: need the two worst-case prompt sets and a peak traffic window from you to re-run an exact staging baseline.
[00:09:58] Priya: I'll upload those to the shared S3 by Monday EOD.
[00:10:05] Martin: We also want a sample rollback runbook — not the full runbook but a 1-page play.
[00:10:11] Maya: We have a template, will tailor and send.
[00:10:20] [00:10:45] --- minutes pass, detailed Q&A on metric definitions and dashboards ---
[00:12:30] Diego: On dashboards — we'll give you token-level cost per route, p50/p95/p99 latency, KV hit rate, and model quality score per route. We can add custom alerts.
[00:12:45] Lena: Important — can we filter by tenant and by route? Our finance folks split cost across products.
[00:12:52] Diego: Yes, per-route and per-API-key cost breakdown is supported. We'll show a demo.
[00:13:05] Martin: Any gotchas on model version pinning? We had an unexpected behavior when mainline model updated.
[00:13:12] Diego: You can pin model versions per route and enforce manual rollouts. Redwood also supports staged rollouts with canary percentages.
[00:13:20] [00:13:50] Priya (leaving): Sorry, need to jump — thanks all, will follow up on the prompt sets.
[00:13:55] Priya: Bye.
[00:14:00] Sophie: Thanks Priya. Remaining — should we agree on the immediate timeline? Diego will run the 24h baseline, Sophie will send pricing, Maya will send runbook template.
[00:14:10] Martin: Sounds good. A short note on ledgering costs — can you give a sample amortization of burst credits in the pricing doc so finance can model?
[00:14:18] Sophie: Absolutely. We'll include an amortization example for burst credits and a quarterly reserved option.
[00:14:25] [00:14:40] Diego: One more technical question from Aaron — do we support in-region private deployment? We want Private offering for some regulated workloads.
[00:14:48] Sophie: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem with KMS integration. We'll include the region availability map in the appendix.
[00:14:55] Aaron: Good.
[00:15:10] [00:15:30] Sophie: Ok let's wrap with recaps.
[00:15:35] Sophie: Recap: 1) Diego runs 24h latency+cost baseline on your staging (needs worst-case prompts and traffic window); 2) Sophie will send pricing tiers, procurement checklist + SLA 1-pager by 2027-08-10; 3) Maya sends a rollback/runbook template; 4) schedule follow-up canary planning meeting once baseline done.
[00:15:55] Martin: Confirming those. One ask — include the impact of quantization and cache hit on sample invoices so finance can model.
[00:16:05] Sophie: We'll include sample invoice slices showing quantization and cache hit adjustments.
[00:16:12] Lena: Great.
[00:16:25] [00:51:30] End notes: final quick chat about calendar invite — Sophie will propose a follow-up the week of Aug 16. Meeting ended at 16:22 local.

References and links mentioned: pricing deck (link to be shared), security appendix (SOC2/KMS), staging baseline spreadsheet (to be uploaded by Redwood), runbook template (Redwood will share).

Quality notes: transcription contains a few mis-hearings and occasional label swaps; technical content verified by SE post-call.
